The trait works at suite level too, and nests: a suite sets the baseline, a test overrides it, and an explicit
stub beats both. Defaults are the fallback of last resort, and they’re scoped — a test without the trait is unaffected by one that has it.

Static requirements have no instance to hang state on, so their spies live in shared storage. Under Swift Testing — which runs tests in parallel by default — that shared storage is a race waiting to happen.
trait solves it by binding fresh, task-local spy storage for the duration of a test.
